title: Logseq vs Obsidian: Which Is Better in 2026?
key_claim: Obsidian scores 9/10 and Logseq 8.4/10; Logseq wins on open-source and free pricing, Obsidian wins on plugin ecosystem and polish.

title: Obsidian vs Logseq: Choosing a Note-Taking App
key_claim: Both use local Markdown files and local storage; Obsidian has 1500+ plugins and handles large vaults better; Logseq excels at outlining, built-in tasks, and PDF annotation.

title: Why I switched from obsidian: A real developer's story and what I'm using now
key_claim: Developer left Obsidian due to sync issues, plugin maintenance burden, and cost; migrated to a simpler markdown-based workflow.

title: Obsidian vs Logseq: which should you choose in 2026?
key_claim: Updated May 2026; Logseq's DB version is a transitional architecture; Obsidian's CLI is a major 2026 differentiator for developers.

title: Logseq vs Obsidian in 2026: Which One Should You Actually Use?
key_claim: Practical comparison from a 5-month daily Logseq user; Logseq's block-centric model suits task management and daily journaling better than Obsidian's page-centric approach.

title: My notes taking app story with markdown, git, VS Code and LLM
key_claim: Plain markdown + git + VS Code + LLM copilot provides a zero-lock-in, scriptable, secure developer knowledge base with three independent backup strategies.

title: Obsidian CLI — Official Documentation
key_claim: Obsidian CLI supports vault operations (create, search, diff, daily notes, tasks), developer commands (eval, devtools, screenshots), and a TUI — all scriptable from the terminal.

title: Obsidian CLI is the new best way to automate your notes
key_claim: CLI enables scheduled note creation, tag migration scripts, and vault-wide operations; currently requires Catalyst license but will become free.
